name: Alexander Graham Bell
hook: The telephone's inventor — and the deaf-education work Jeopardy remembers him for.

facts.label: the telephone
facts.statement: Bell patented the telephone in 1876 (patent No. 174,465), beating rival Elisha Gray by only a few hours; it was called the most valuable patent ever issued.

facts.label: Thomas Watson
facts.statement: On March 10, 1876, Bell called his assistant Thomas Watson on the new telephone and later made him a partner in the Bell Telephone Company.

facts.label: Helen Keller
facts.statement: Helen Keller dedicated The Story of My Life to Bell, who examined her at age 6 and taught the deaf to speak.

facts.label: Scotland and Canada
facts.statement: Bell was born in Scotland in 1847 and died in Canada in 1922; his Nova Scotia site is a historic site.

facts.label: decibel
facts.statement: The decibel, a unit of sound intensity abbreviated dB, is named for Alexander Graham Bell.

facts.label: metal detector
facts.statement: Bell built an early metal detector to locate the bullet in President James Garfield, but mattress springs confused it.

facts.label: tetrahedral kites
facts.statement: In 1901 Bell began building tetrahedral box kites with the goal of lifting people.
